title: Computational Complexity
tagline: Time complexity, P and NP, NP-completeness, coping with intractability, space complexity, the polynomial hierarchy, randomised computation and the PCP theorem
summary: Complexity theory asks which problems can be solved efficiently, and gives strong evidence that many cannot. This course defines time and space complexity classes, develops the theory of NP-completeness through polynomial-time reductions, surveys ways of coping with intractable problems, and studies space-bounded, randomised and approximate computation, ending with the PCP theorem and the hardness of approximation.

chapters.title: Time complexity and the class P
chapters.summary: Measuring time on Turing machines, polynomial time and why the class P is robust.

chapters.title: The class NP
chapters.summary: Nondeterministic time, verifiers and certificates, and the P versus NP question.

chapters.title: NP-completeness and the Cook–Levin theorem
chapters.summary: Polynomial-time reductions, NP-hardness and the NP-completeness of satisfiability.

chapters.title: A catalogue of NP-complete problems
chapters.summary: Reductions to 3-SAT, clique, vertex cover, Hamiltonian cycle, subset sum and graph colouring.

chapters.title: Coping with intractability
chapters.summary: Exact exponential algorithms, fixed-parameter tractability, SAT solvers and heuristics.

chapters.title: Space complexity
chapters.summary: PSPACE, Savitch’s theorem, PSPACE-completeness and logarithmic space.

chapters.title: Hierarchy theorems and the polynomial hierarchy
chapters.summary: Time and space hierarchy theorems, oracles and relativisation, and the polynomial hierarchy.

chapters.title: Randomised computation
chapters.summary: Probabilistic Turing machines, the classes BPP, RP and ZPP, and derandomisation.

chapters.title: Approximation and the PCP theorem
chapters.summary: Approximation algorithms and ratios, the PCP theorem and the hardness of approximation.
